title: Construct Machine Spec v1
description: The checked breakdown of an English requirement into states, events, guarded transitions and typed functions (#576, R1). English goes in as an ordered list of sentences, each with an id; every state, event, transition and function carries a `req` list naming the sentence(s) it came from, and a sentence that deliberately produces nothing is listed under `outOfScope` with a reason -- so `construct research spec <file>` can refuse a spec that silently dropped a sentence, invented an item no sentence asked for, or cannot be turned into a real machine (an unreachable state, a transition to a state or event that does not exist, a function without types). Drafting one is the only fuzzy step (a person, a form, or a model given this schema plus examples/machine-spec.v1.example.json -- never prose instructions); everything after it is deterministic: packages/core/research/machine-spec.mjs runs the checks, and the sibling R2 slice turns an accepted spec into the state union, the XState machine (`states[].id` are the machine's state keys, `events[].id` its event types, `transitions[]` its `on` map with `guard` names, `functions[]` its typed stubs). Additive data goes in the free-form `ext` object; a breaking shape change creates machine-spec.v2 rather than mutating v1 in place.

version.description: Spec schema version. Bump to v2 on any breaking shape change.

name.description: What the machine is called in plain words (e.g. "sign-in with retry"). The generated workflow unit's name is derived from it.

feature.description: Optional: the Construct feature the machine belongs to (features/<feature>/workflows/). The generating command can also take it as a flag.

requirement.description: The English requirement, split into sentences in reading order. Ids are what every other item's `req` points at; the text is kept verbatim so the read-back can diff against it.

outOfScope.description: Sentences that deliberately produce no state, event, transition or function, each with the reason. A sentence must be either covered by some item's `req` or listed here -- never both, never neither.

states.description: The machine's states. Exactly one is `initial`; every state must be reachable from it through `transitions`.

events.description: Every event a transition may name. `payload` is the TypeScript type of the event's data, if any.

transitions.description: Directed edges: in state `from`, on `event`, go to `to` -- only when `guard` (a named boolean condition, if given) holds.

functions.description: The functions the machine needs, each fully typed (TypeScript type strings) and framed by a precondition and a postcondition in plain words. These become the typed stubs and their unit tests.

ext.description: Reserved free-form extension object, ignored by validators.

id.description: A non-empty identifier with no leading or trailing whitespace. Unique within its own list.

req.description: The requirement sentence(s) this item was derived from. Every id must exist in `requirement`.

typeString.description: A TypeScript type written as source text, e.g. "Credentials", "Promise<Session | null>", "void".

reason.description: Why, in plain words (e.g. "a non-functional constraint, checked by a rule instead").

id.description: The state key in the generated machine.

initial.description: True on exactly one state: where the machine starts.

final.description: True when the machine stops here; a final state has no outgoing transitions.

description.description: Optional one line for the read-back.

id.description: The event type in the generated machine (e.g. "SUBMIT").

payload.description: Optional TypeScript type of the event's data.

id.description: Optional stable id for traceability; unique among transitions when given.

guard.description: Optional name of the boolean condition that must hold for this transition to be taken. Two transitions with the same from/event/guard are ambiguous and refused.

name.description: A valid TypeScript identifier; the exported function's name.

output.description: The return type (use "void" for none; wrap async results in Promise<...>).

precondition.description: What must be true before the call, in plain words.

postcondition.description: What is true after the call, in plain words; the generated unit test asserts it.
